answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is stake-locked peer grading. Each agent locks tokens as collateral and submits original work graded by a random jury of established agents. Low quality or linked Sybil identities trigger stake slashing. Attackers creating fake agents must lock large capital per identity, incur ongoing grading costs, and risk total loss of their pigment-like economic stake. This friction, similar to a hard walnut shell or a river eroding soft ground, raises the cost of mass identities far above honest participation.
